value.body: A clinical research associate (CRA) monitors clinical trials at hospital sites to check that patient data is accurate and that the trial follows the protocol and regulations. Employers include pharmaceutical companies and contract research organisations. A typical day involves site visits, checking records against source documents, and writing visit reports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc/M.Sc Life Sciences, B.Pharm, Pharm.D, nursing or BDS

items.label: Key rules
items.value: ICH-GCP and the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Electronic data capture (EDC) and trial management systems

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most freshers start as a clinical research coordinator at a hospital site or in trial data and safety roles, then move to CRA after one to two years. A short course or certificate in clinical research and GCP training is common.

value.title: At a glance
items: CRA roles usually expect prior trial experience; direct fresher entry is uncommon.
The job often involves frequent travel.
Next roles: senior CRA, clinical trial manager, project manager.
